summary: PayStream: inference shard stall cascade causing streaming timeouts and routing loops (major customer escalation)
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 19:02 UTC, PayStream experienced degraded streaming responses and intermittent 5xx errors. Customers reported long stalls (10-30s) during streaming completions followed by client disconnects. The user's SDK observed repeated reconnects and routed requests repeatedly to the same serving shard, triggering a routing loop that amplified the outage for several minutes. Impact: Broad streaming timeouts for a high-throughput dedicated customer; measurable SLO breach for streaming latency and error rate. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (paystream-dc-us-east-1), autoscaled scheduler, routing policy pinned to low-latency shards. Timeline: 19:02 UTC first alerts on increased streaming tail latency; 19:07 escalation to SEV0 when customer reported production failures; mitigation and rollback actions executed by 20:05 UTC; service returned to steady-state by 20:40 UTC. This ticket captures the incident, investigation notes, and post-incident follow-up items.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send long-streaming chat requests (context ~8k tokens) against PayStream's pinned model endpoint under steady load. 2) Observe that some requests start streaming but stall mid-output for 10+ seconds. 3) Retry behavior in SDK sometimes triggers routing to same shard which is in a degraded state. 4) Repeated retries produce correlated backlog and 5xx responses. Note: Reproduction depends on load and pinned shard topology; not observed in ephemeral shared endpoints.
impact: PayStream reported 15-25% of streaming requests either stalled or failed with 5xx over a 45-minute window. Customer visible impact: timeouts in their payment flow horizon, automated retries caused billing spikes and increased token usage. Business impact: dedicated customer SLA exposure and an executive escalation from PayStream security/ops.
logs:
Excerpted errors from serving-runtime logs: 
[2026-03-10T19:05:12Z] ERROR shard=shard-17 kvcache=miss stream=conn-93 stall_detected=1 stall_duration_ms=12345
[2026-03-10T19:05:14Z] WARN scheduler:enqueue backlog=482 target_shard=shard-17 owner=paystream
[2026-03-10T19:06:01Z] ERROR gateway:502 upstream=shard-17 reason=handler-timeout
Connection traces show repeated keepalive resets and TCP retransmits. Observability metrics: per-shard inflight tokens spiked to 6x baseline for shard-17; router showed increased prefailure reroute count for the paystream route.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor or GPU stall on shard causing long KV cache stall and backpressure through the scheduler. Evidence: single shard (shard-17) showed disproportionate inflight and stall metrics; kernel-level traces indicated an occasional CUDA page fault on the node hosting shard-17 (node node-gpu-05). Secondary finding: routing policy pinned PayStream's route to low-latency shards with sticky session affinity; retries in the SDK were not circuit-broken quickly, which produced repeated traffic to the degraded shard. Actions taken during investigation: 1) SRE moved active routing for PayStream to warm spare shards at 19:18 UTC. 2) Autoscaler increased pool capacity and drained node-gpu-05 for inspection. 3) Engineering collected kernel dmesg and nvml logs; preliminary NVML logs showed a transient driver hiccup and soft ECC correction events on node-gpu-05 around 19:04 UTC. 4) A temporary SDK guidance was posted to customer to reduce aggressive retry behavior. Correlated entries: slack #inc-support-paystream thread (https://slack.redwood.ai/incidents/CLX12345), telemetry dashboard (permalink: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/paystream-2026-03-10).
resolution: Mitigations applied: 1) Immediate routing diversion off shard-17 to healthy shards and tightened retry circuit-breaker for PayStream (19:18 UTC). 2) Node-gpu-05 removed from pool and rebooted; driver upgraded from 525.60 to 525.76 as precaution (19:50 UTC). 3) Autoscaler increased reserved warm capacity for the customer's dedicated pool to reduce single-shard pressure. 4) A rolling patch was deployed to the scheduler to accelerate shard rebalancing under detected stall signals (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789) and a hotfix to router retry logic to add jitter and a fast-circuit open path (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/412). Service observed steady-state at ~20:40 UTC.
resolution_notes: Root cause (provisional): transient GPU driver/firmware glitch on node-gpu-05 triggered soft ECC corrections and occasional stalls in model execution paths leading to prolonged KV cache stalls. Contributing factors: aggressive sticky routing + customer SDK retry policy amplified load to the single degraded shard. Follow-ups (owners and ETA): 1) infra-team: schedule EV kernel/driver health sweep across all GPU nodes and add ECC anomaly alerting (Owner: Priya Rao, due 2026-03-20). 2) runtime-team: add explicit shard-stall detector that will trigger proactive rebalancing sooner (Owner: Marco Chen, due 2026-03-24). 3) support/solutions: publish SDK retry guidance and introduce client-side exponential backoff defaults for streaming (Owner: Elena Morales, due 2026-03-17). 4) account & CS: provide PayStream with incident timeline, cost-impact estimate, and credit recommendation (Owner: Ben Thompson, due 2026-03-16).
